verdict: Apple set a September-quarter record: revenue rose 8% to $102.5B as Services hit an all-time high of $28.8B, and profit reached $27.5B.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: +91% vs a tax-hit year-ago quarter; +13% adjusted

segments.name: iPhone
segments.note: A September-quarter record for iPhone; the iPhone 17 lineup launched in the final week of the quarter.

segments.name: Wearables, Home and Accessories
segments.note: Apple Watch, AirPods, HomePod and accessories; flat YoY.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: The App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, Apple TV, Apple Pay and warranties — an all-time record, up 15% YoY, and Apple's highest-margin business.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing future products and software; up 14% YoY as Apple invests in AI and new devices.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling and admin costs, including Apple's stores; up 8% YoY.

otherDetail: Other income (expense), net was +$377M: interest and dividend income exceeded interest expense and other items.
follow100Note: The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Services set another all-time high
takeaways.text: Services reached $28.8B, up 15%, and it is Apple's most profitable money: delivering those services cost $7.1B, against $47.0B of cost on $73.7B of product sales. The installed base of active devices hit a new all-time high.

takeaways.title: A record fiscal year
takeaways.text: Fiscal 2025 revenue was a record $416.2B and net income was $112.0B. Apple bought back $90.7B of its own stock during the year.

takeaways.title: EPS growth, on a like-for-like basis
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS of $1.85 is up 91% — but only because the year-ago quarter absorbed a $10.2B one-time tax charge. Excluding that charge from the comparison, Apple says EPS grew 13%.

oneTimers: The year-ago comparison is distorted: in Q4 FY24 Apple booked a one-time $10.2B income-tax charge after the European Commission's State Aid decision was reinstated, which cut that quarter's EPS to $0.97. This quarter's GAAP EPS of $1.85 is up 91% against it; on the adjusted basis Apple cites, EPS grew 13%.
